implementation_supports.text: Set a ten-minute timer and take the smallest visible step toward this.
Write the next action as one sentence starting with a concrete verb, then do only that step.
Choose a specific day and place for one brief first attempt.
Put one needed material, link, or contact detail where it will be ready.
Remove one small source of friction before trying the action.
Ask one supportive person for a brief check-in after you try it.
Try a low-stakes version once and treat it as information, not a test.

Pair a five-minute version with an existing daily or weekly cue.

hows.text: Send them a text asking how they have been.
Send a short voice note saying you would like to reconnect.

close-relationships.what: Make more room for family connection.

hows.text: Invite one family member to share a meal or call.
Start a small recurring ritual such as a Sunday check-in.
Send a photo or memory with a short note.
Write down the impact you want to acknowledge before speaking.
Ask whether the person is open to a short conversation.
Offer one specific apology or repair without demanding a response.

close-relationships.what: Practice clearer boundaries with people I love.

hows.text: Write one boundary in a calm one-sentence form.
Choose a low-stakes situation in which to practice saying no.
Ask for time to think before agreeing to a request.
List the recurring tasks that currently need attention.
Ask for a ten-minute conversation about one uneven responsibility.

close-relationships.what: Be more present during time together.

hows.text: Put devices out of reach during one conversation or meal.
Notice when attention drifts and gently return to the person.
Choose one shared activity and give it your full attention.
Greet the people you live with before starting another task.
Make one shared space comfortable for a relaxed conversation.
Offer a small gesture of welcome when someone arrives.

close-relationships.what: Support a caregiver or family member.

hows.text: Ask what kind of practical help would actually be useful.
Offer one bounded task you can realistically complete.
Schedule a short check-in that also respects your own limits.

close-relationships.what: Talk about something that matters to me.

hows.text: Write down the main point and one feeling before the conversation.

close-relationships.what: Learn more about someone close to me.

hows.text: Ask what has been taking most of their attention lately.

Invite one friend to coffee, a walk, or a short call this week.

friendship.what: Meet people around a shared interest.

friendship.what: Share more play and enjoyment with others.

friendship.what: Offer practical support to a friend.

hows.text: Ask whether listening or practical help would be more useful.

friendship.what: Let friends know me more accurately.

hows.text: Share one genuine preference instead of automatically agreeing.

work-education.what: Make progress on one meaningful work or study priority.

work-education.what: Learn a useful skill for my role.

hows.text: Choose one tutorial, chapter, or lesson and schedule thirty minutes.

work-education.what: Contribute more clearly in meetings or classes.

hows.text: Write down one point or question before the next meeting.

work-education.what: Improve the quality of a recurring task.
